your phone connects to the proxylink app on your pc over the local network (wss, a websocket over tls). files and text go through the pc, phones do not connect to each other. nothing goes through a cloud or an outside server

the connection is encrypted with tls. the app trusts only the pc certificate whose sha-256 fingerprint was saved at pairing, the host name is not checked. the data is decrypted on the pc, so this is not end-to-end encryption between phones

pairing needs a one-time code from the pc (qr code or six digits) or a guest token. a link opened from nfc or another app asks you first. after pairing, the phone proves itself with a shared secret on every connection. received files are checked with a sha-256 checksum
what is saved on the phone

paired devices (name, certificate fingerprint and the shared secret), settings, the list of received and sent items and, only if you turn it on, the clipboard history. the secret is kept in the private storage of the app and is not encrypted by the app itself. automatic backup of the app is turned off
how long and where to delete

the clipboard history follows the limits in the clipboard settings. the list of items can be cleared in transfers. a paired device and its secret stay until you forget it. clipboard content and the secret are not written to diagnostics, and the app writes no logs

internet and network state: connect to the pc and find it on the network. camera: scan the qr code. nfc: read a pairing tag. notifications: show received items and requests. foreground service and wake lock: keep the connection alive. start after reboot and battery optimization: optional. location and nearby wi-fi: only for the hotspot. the current state of each permission is in privacy
the app has no analytics, advertising or telemetry code of its own, no account and no cloud. the qr scanner uses the Google ML Kit library, its own behavior is not covered by this statement
